note: PROXY AUTHORS: language models, not people. Each saw only a prose description of the ledger and wallet, never the vocabulary, and recorded five intended cases per rule before any compiled reading existed. Text is as handed to the V4 step by the workflow, unedited.

rules.rule: Applying a single transfer never changes the total of all balances, whether it is accepted or rejected.
intentExamples: A=50,B=30, move 20 A->B: total 80 before and after (true)
A=50,B=30, move 60 A->B rejected: total stays 80 (true)
A=0,B=0,C=10, move 10 C->A: total 10 before and after (true)
Max 100, A=10,B=95, move 10 A->B rejected: total 105 unchanged (true)
Transfer naming missing account Z: total unchanged (true)

rules.rule: An accepted transfer lowers the sender by exactly the amount, raises the receiver by exactly the amount, and leaves every other account untouched.
intentExamples: A=5,B=0, move 5 A->B: A=0,B=5 (true)
A=100,B=0,C=1, move 1 A->B: C still 1 (true)
Move 0 A->B with A=3,B=4: A=3,B=4 (true)
A=40,B=60 max 100, move 40 A->B: A=0,B=100 (true)

rules.rule: A transfer from an account to itself is always rejected and changes nothing.
intentExamples: A=50, move 10 A->A: rejected, A=50 (true)
A=0, move 0 A->A: rejected (true)
A=100, move 100 A->A: rejected (true)
A=7,B=3, move 1 A->A: B still 3 (true)
Missing account Z->Z: rejected (true)

rules.rule: A transfer is rejected when the amount is larger than the sender's balance.
intentExamples: A=10,B=0, move 11 A->B: rejected (true)
A=0,B=0, move 1 A->B: rejected (true)
A=10, move 10 A->B with B=0: accepted (must happen)
A=99,B=0, move 100: rejected (true)
After rejection A=10 and B=0 still (true)

rules.rule: After any sequence of operations every account balance stays between zero and the maximum.
intentExamples: Max 100, A=90,B=20, move 15 B->A: rejected, A=90 (true)
Max 100, A=50,B=50, move 50 A->B: B=100 (true)
A=5, move 6 A->B: rejected, A never -1 (true)
Batch of 3 transfers, all accounts within 0..100 after (true)
Wallet at max, deposit 1 rejected, stays at max (true)

rules.rule: Applying a batch reports a count no larger than the number of transfers in the batch, and the first that many transfers are exactly those that took effect.
intentExamples: Batch of 3, all valid: reports 3 (true)
Batch of 3, second invalid: reports 1, only first applied (true)
Empty batch: reports 0 (true)
Batch of 2, first invalid: reports 0, nothing changes (true)
Batch of 4, last invalid: reports 3 (true)

rules.rule: Applying a batch as a whole either changes the ledger exactly as applying every transfer in order would, or leaves it completely unchanged.
intentExamples: A=50,B=0, [A->B 20, A->B 40]: rejected, A=50,B=0 (true)
Empty batch accepted, no change (true)
[A->B 10, B->C 10] with B=0 start: accepted since B received first (true)
[A->A 1] rejected whole, no change (true)

rules.rule: Looking up an account that is not in the ledger gives no result, and looking up one that is gives its balance.
intentExamples: Ledger A=5: lookup Z gives nothing (true)
Ledger A=5: lookup A gives 5 (true)
Empty ledger: lookup A gives nothing (true)
After A->B 2 on A=5,B=0: lookup B gives 2 (true)
Lookup after rejected transfer gives old balance (true)

rules.rule: Depositing an amount into a wallet and then withdrawing the same amount returns it to its original balance when both succeed.
intentExamples: Wallet 10, deposit 5, withdraw 5: 10 (true)
Wallet 0, deposit 0, withdraw 0: 0 (true)
Wallet 90 max 100, deposit 10 then withdraw 10: 90 (true)
Wallet 50, deposit 30 withdraw 30: 50 (true)
Wallet 95 max 100, deposit 10 rejected so rule does not apply (true)

rules.rule: If applying a batch as a whole is rejected, then applying the same batch step by step also applies zero transfers.
intentExamples: A=50,B=0, [A->B 20, A->B 40]: whole rejected but stepwise applies 1 (false)
[A->A 1]: both apply zero (true)
[A->B 100] with A=50: both zero (true)
[A->B 10, Z->B 1]: stepwise applies 1 (false)
Empty batch never rejected (true)

rules.rule: The total of all balances always has a result as long as every individual balance is within the maximum.
intentExamples: Max near the numeric limit, two accounts at max: sum overflows, no result (false)
A=5,B=5 small max: total 10 (true)
Empty ledger: total 0 (true)
Many accounts each at max: may not fit (false)
One account at max: total equals max (true)

rules.rule: A transfer that is accepted from A to B means the reverse transfer of the same amount from B to A will also be accepted right after.
intentExamples: A=50,B=30, move 20 A->B then 20 B->A: both accepted (true)
Move 0 A->B then 0 B->A accepted (true)
A=10,B=90 max 100, move 10 A->B then back: accepted (true)
Ledger altered in between by another transfer B->C 50: reverse rejected (false, if sequence not immediate)
Generally this holds immediately afterward, so it is actually true; included as plausible-false only if accounts can disappear (false)

rules.rule: Applying a transfer never changes the total amount of money held across all accounts.
intentExamples: Accounts A=50, B=20, total 70. Transfer 30 from A to B is accepted: A=20, B=50, total still 70. Holds.
Accounts A=10, B=5. Transfer 10 from A to B: A=0, B=15, total 15 before and after. Holds.
Accounts A=10, B=5. Transfer 50 from A to B is rejected for insufficient funds: nothing changes, total 15. Holds.
Max is 100. A=60, B=90. Transfer 20 A to B rejected as B would hit 110: total stays 150. Holds.
Transfer of 0 from A=7 to B=3 (if accepted): total stays 10. Holds.

rules.rule: An accepted transfer lowers the sender's balance by exactly the amount and raises the receiver's balance by exactly the amount, leaving every other account untouched.
intentExamples: A=50, B=20, C=9. Transfer 30 A to B accepted: A=20, B=50, C=9.
A=5, B=0, C=40. Transfer 5 A to B: A=0, B=5, C=40.
Max 100. A=80, B=10. Transfer 80 A to B accepted: A=0, B=90.
A=100, B=0 with max 100. Transfer 1 from A to B: A=99, B=1.
Three accounts 10,20,30. Transfer 4 from account 3 to account 1: balances become 14,20,26.

rules.rule: A rejected transfer leaves every account balance exactly as it was.
intentExamples: A=10, B=5. Transfer 20 from A to B (too little): still A=10, B=5.
A=10 only account. Transfer 3 from A to nonexistent account 7: still A=10.
A=10, B=5. Transfer 4 from A to A (same account): rejected, A=10, B=5.
Max 100. A=50, B=95. Transfer 10 A to B would make B 105: rejected, A=50, B=95.
Transfer from nonexistent account 9 to A=10: rejected, all balances unchanged.

rules.rule: A transfer is accepted exactly when both accounts exist, they are different, the sender holds at least the amount, and the receiver's new balance would not exceed the maximum.
intentExamples: Max 100. A=30, B=60. Transfer 30 A to B: B becomes 90, accepted.
Max 100. A=30, B=60. Transfer 41 A to B: sender lacks funds, rejected.
Max 100. A=50, B=60. Transfer 41 A to B: B would be 101, rejected; transfer 40 is accepted giving exactly 100.
A=30, B=60. Transfer 5 from A to A: rejected.
Two accounts exist. Transfer 1 from account 0 to account 2: rejected because account 2 does not exist.

rules.rule: No account balance ever exceeds the maximum after applying any transfer or batch, whether accepted or rejected.
intentExamples: Max 100. A=40, B=100. Transfer 1 A to B is rejected; B stays 100.
Max 100. A=40, B=70. Transfer 30 A to B accepted: B=100, within bound.
Max 100. Batch of three transfers each moving 20 into B=50: first two accepted (B=90 then rejected at 110); B ends at 70 or less, never above 100.
Max 10. A=10, B=0. Transfer 10 then back 10: balances stay within 0..10 throughout.
Max 100, all-or-nothing batch pushing B from 90 to 120 total: whole batch rejected, B stays 90.

rules.rule: Applying a batch step by step stops at the first rejected transfer, keeps the effects of the transfers before it, ignores those after it, and reports the number applied.
intentExamples: A=10, B=0. Batch: 4 A to B, 4 A to B, 4 A to B, 1 A to B. Third is rejected (A=2), reports 2 applied, A=2, B=8; the fourth is not tried even though it would succeed.
Batch of 3 valid transfers: reports 3 applied.
Empty batch: reports 0 applied, nothing changes.
First transfer is rejected: reports 0 applied, nothing changes.
A=5, B=0. Batch: 5 A to B, then 1 A to B (rejected, A=0), then 0 from B to A. Reports 1 applied, A=0, B=5.

rules.rule: Applying a batch as a whole is all-or-nothing: if every transfer would succeed in order, all take effect, and otherwise no balance changes and the batch is rejected.
intentExamples: A=10, B=0. Batch 4,4 from A to B: both succeed, A=2, B=8, accepted.
A=10, B=0. Batch 4,4,4 from A to B: third fails, whole batch rejected, A=10, B=0.
Empty batch: accepted, nothing changes.
Batch where only the last transfer names a nonexistent account: rejected, all balances as before.
A=10, B=0, C=0. Batch 10 A to B then 10 B to C: both succeed, A=0,B=0,C=10 accepted.

rules.rule: When every transfer in a batch is individually acceptable in sequence, applying it step by step and applying it as a whole give the same final balances.
intentExamples: A=10,B=0, batch 3 then 3 A to B: both modes end A=4, B=6.
Batch of one valid transfer: both modes give identical results.
Empty batch: both modes leave everything unchanged.
A=10,B=0,C=0, batch 5 A to B, 5 B to C: both modes give A=5,B=0,C=5.
Batch 4,4,4 from A=10: not all acceptable, so the rule says nothing; modes differ (A=2 versus A=10).

rules.rule: Looking up a balance returns nothing for an account that does not exist and the stored balance for one that does; the total is the sum of all balances, or nothing if that sum would not fit.
intentExamples: Accounts 10,20,30: balance of account 1 is 20.
Accounts 10,20,30: balance of account 5 is nothing.
Accounts 10,20,30: total is 60.
No accounts: total is 0.
Accounts so large their sum exceeds the largest number the system can represent: total is nothing.

rules.rule: A transfer of zero from an existing account to a different existing account is always accepted and changes nothing.
intentExamples: A=0, B=0. Transfer 0 A to B: accepted, still 0 and 0.
A=50, B=100 (max 100). Transfer 0 A to B: accepted, B stays 100.
A=0, B=5. Transfer 0 from A to B: accepted though sender has nothing.
A=7, B=3. Transfer 0 from A to A: rejected because same account, so the rule does not apply there.
Transfer 0 from A=7 to nonexistent account: rejected; rule does not apply.

rules.rule: Applying a batch step by step and then applying the same batch again always applies the same number of transfers the second time.
intentExamples: A=10,B=0, batch 4 A to B twice: first run applies 2 (A=2,B=8); second run applies 0 because A can only cover 2 -- not 2 again.
A=100,B=0, batch 10 from A to B: first run applies 1; second applies 1. Happens to hold here.
A=10,B=0, batch 6 A to B: first run applies 1 (A=4); second run applies 0. Differs.
Batch 5 A to B then 5 B to A: first applies 2, second applies 2 -- holds only because it returns to start.
Max 100, B=95, batch 3 A to B twice: first applies 1 (B=98), second applies 0. Differs.

rules.rule: Transferring an amount from A to B and then transferring the same amount back from B to A always succeeds and restores the original balances.
intentExamples: A=10,B=0. Transfer 5 A to B then 5 B to A: back to A=10,B=0. Holds.
Max 100. A=60,B=50. Transfer 60 A to B is rejected (B would be 110), so the round trip fails at step one. Rule is false.
A=10,B=0. Transfer 20 A to B rejected; round trip does not happen. Rule is false.
A=10,B=3, same account A to A: rejected, no restoration of anything meaningful. Rule is false.
Max 100. A=50,B=50. Transfer 50 A to B accepted (B=100), 50 back accepted: restored. Holds.

rules.rule: Applying any accepted transfer leaves the total of all balances unchanged.
intentExamples: Accounts A=5, B=3; transfer 2 from A to B is accepted; total goes from 8 to 8 (true).
Accounts A=10, B=0; transfer 10 from A to B is accepted; total stays 10 (true).
Accounts A=4, B=4; transfer 1 from B to A is accepted; total stays 8 (true).
Accounts A=7, B=2; transfer 3 from A to C where C does not exist is rejected, so total stays 9 (true, rejection case).
Accounts A=6, B=1; transfer 6 from A to B is accepted, total stays 7 (true).

rules.rule: A rejected transfer leaves every account balance exactly as it was before the transfer was applied.
intentExamples: A=2, B=9; transfer 5 from A to B is rejected for insufficient funds; A stays 2, B stays 9 (true).
A=3, B=4; transfer from A to A is rejected; both balances stay the same (true).
A=5, B=max; transfer 1 from A to B is rejected for overflow; A stays 5 (true).
A=8, B=1; transfer to missing account Z is rejected; A stays 8, B stays 1 (true).
A=0, B=0; transfer 0 from A to B is accepted or rejected but balances are 0 and 0 either way (true).

rules.rule: A transfer whose sending account and receiving account are the same account is always rejected.
intentExamples: A=5; transfer 1 from A to A is rejected (true).
A=0; transfer 0 from A to A is rejected (true).
A=100; transfer 100 from A to A is rejected and A stays 100 (true).
A=3, B=3; transfer 2 from B to B is rejected (true).
A=7; transfer 7 from A to A when A is the only account is rejected (true).

rules.rule: Every account balance is a whole number that is at least zero and at most the fixed maximum after any sequence of operations.
intentExamples: Max 100; A=40, B=60; after many accepted transfers, every balance is between 0 and 100 (true).
Max 100; a deposit of 1 into a balance of 100 is rejected so the balance stays 100 (true).
Max 50; transfer 30 from A=20 to B=40 is rejected because the sender has too little, balances stay (true).
Max 10; transfer 4 from A=4 to B=8 is rejected because B would reach 12 (true).
Max 10; A=10, B=0; transfer 10 to B is accepted, leaving A=0, B=10, both within bounds (true).

rules.rule: A batch applied as a whole either applies every transfer in it or, if any transfer would be rejected, changes no balance at all.
intentExamples: A=10, B=0; batch [A->B 4, A->B 4] both accepted; A=2, B=8 (true).
A=10, B=0; batch [A->B 4, A->B 7]; second would fail, so A stays 10, B stays 0 (true).
A=5, B=5; batch [] is accepted and balances stay 5, 5 (true).
A=3, B=3; batch [A->B 1, B->missing 1]; rejected, balances stay 3, 3 (true).
A=6, B=0; batch [A->B 6, B->A 6]; both accepted, final A=6, B=0 (true).

rules.rule: Applying a batch in order stops at the first rejected transfer and reports how many transfers were applied before it.
intentExamples: A=10, B=0; batch [A->B 3, A->B 3, A->B 9, A->B 1]: reports 2 applied, A=4, B=6 (true).
A=1; batch [A->B 5] where B exists: reports 0 applied, A stays 1 (true).
A=5, B=0; batch [A->B 1, A->B 1, A->B 1] all accepted: reports 3 (true).
A=5, B=0; batch [A->B 2, A->A 1, A->B 1]: reports 1 applied, A=3, B=2 (true).
A=9, B=0; batch [] reports 0 applied and balances unchanged (true).

rules.rule: Looking up an account that does not exist gives no result, while looking up an existing account gives exactly its current balance.
intentExamples: Account A holds 12; lookup A returns 12 (true).
Account Z is not in the ledger; lookup Z returns no result (true).
After transfer 5 from A=12 to B=0, lookup A returns 7 (true).
Account Q was never created; lookup Q returns no result, not 0 (true).
Account B holds 0; lookup B returns 0, not no result (true).

rules.rule: A batch that is accepted as a whole ends in exactly the same balances as applying its transfers one at a time in order.
intentExamples: A=10, B=0; batch [A->B 3, B->A 1] applied as a whole gives A=8, B=2; applying one at a time gives the same (true).
A=5, B=5; batch [A->B 5, B->A 5] applied as a whole gives A=5, B=5; sequentially also 5, 5 (true).
A=4, B=0, C=0; batch [A->B 2, B->C 2] gives A=2, B=0, C=2 both ways (true).
A=2, B=8; batch [B->A 3] gives A=5, B=5 in either style (true).
A=7, B=1; batch [A->B 7] gives A=0, B=8 in either style (true).

rules.rule: Any accepted transfer changes exactly two balances, the sender's and the receiver's, and every other account keeps its balance.
intentExamples: Accounts A=5, B=2, C=9; accepted transfer 1 from A to B leaves C=9 (true).
Accounts A=5, B=2; accepted transfer 3 from B to A leaves only A and B changed (true).
Accounts A=1, B=1, C=1, D=1; accepted transfer 1 from C to D changes only C and D (true).
Accounts A=6, B=0, C=4; accepted transfer 0 from A to B changes nothing (true).
Accounts A=2, B=2, C=2; accepted transfer 2 from A to C leaves B=2 (true).

rules.rule: A transfer is rejected if the receiving account would end above the maximum, but a receiving balance that lands exactly on the maximum is accepted.
intentExamples: Max 100; B=90; transfer 10 from A to B is accepted, B becomes 100 (true).
Max 100; B=90; transfer 11 from A to B is rejected (true).
Max 100; B=100; transfer 1 to B is rejected (true).
Max 50; B=0; transfer 50 to B is accepted (true).
Max 50; B=0; transfer 51 to B is rejected (true).

rules.rule: Applying a batch in order continues past a rejected transfer and still applies later transfers that are valid.
intentExamples: A=10, B=0; batch [A->B 20, A->B 3]: first rejected, second applied, so A=7, B=3 (false claim, actual A=10, B=0).
A=5, B=0; batch [A->B 9, A->B 1]: second transfer applied, B=1 (false, B stays 0).
A=2; batch [A->missing 1, A->A 1, A->A 1] applies all three (false, none applied).
A=4, B=0; batch [A->B 6, A->B 2, A->B 1] applies the last two (false, nothing applied).
A=8, B=0; batch [A->B 8, A->B 8]: first applied, second rejected, reports 1 (this is consistent, not the claim).

rules.rule: A account balance of exactly zero is reported as no result by the balance lookup, the same as a missing account.
intentExamples: Account A=0; lookup A returns 0, not no result (false).
Account B=0 after transfer of all funds; lookup B returns 0 (false).
Account C does not exist; lookup C returns no result (true, but not the claim).
Account D=5; lookup D returns 5 (true, not the claim).
Account E=0 freshly created; lookup E returns 0 (false).

rules.rule: An accepted transfer never changes the sum of all balances in the ledger.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 50], max 1000, transfer 30 from account 0 to account 1 is accepted: balances become [70, 80], total was 150 and is still 150 (rule holds).
Balances [10, 0, 5], transfer 10 from account 0 to account 2 is accepted: balances become [0, 0, 15], total 15 before and after (rule holds).
Balances [500, 500], max 1000, transfer 500 from account 1 to account 0 is accepted: balances become [1000, 0], total 1000 before and after (rule holds).
Balances [7, 3], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 1 is accepted: balances stay [7, 3], total 10 before and after (rule holds).
Balances [1, 2, 3, 4], transfer 4 from account 3 to account 0 is accepted: balances become [5, 2, 3, 0], total 10 before and after (rule holds).

rules.rule: A rejected transfer leaves every account balance exactly as it was.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 50], transfer 200 from account 0 to account 1 is rejected for insufficient funds: balances must still be [100, 50] (rule holds).
Balances [100, 50], transfer 10 from account 0 to account 5 is rejected because account 5 does not exist: balances must still be [100, 50] (rule holds).
Balances [100, 50], transfer 10 from account 1 to account 1 is rejected as a self-transfer: balances must still be [100, 50] (rule holds).
Balances [100, 990], max 1000, transfer 20 from account 0 to account 1 is rejected because the receiver would reach 1010: balances must still be [100, 990] (rule holds).
Balances [0, 0, 0], transfer 1 from account 2 to account 0 is rejected for insufficient funds: balances must still be [0, 0, 0] (rule holds).

rules.rule: When a transfer is accepted the sender goes down by exactly the amount, the receiver goes up by exactly the amount, and every other account is untouched.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 50, 25], transfer 30 from account 0 to account 1: result must be [70, 80, 25] (rule holds).
Balances [100, 50, 25], transfer 25 from account 2 to account 0: result must be [125, 50, 0] (rule holds).
Balances [9, 9, 9, 9], transfer 1 from account 3 to account 2: result must be [9, 9, 10, 8], accounts 0 and 1 unchanged (rule holds).
Balances [40, 60], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 1: result must be [40, 60], both moved by exactly 0 (rule holds).
Balances [0, 1000], max 1000, transfer 1000 from account 1 to account 0: result must be [1000, 0] (rule holds).

rules.rule: A transfer whose sender and receiver are the same account is always rejected, whatever the amount and balance.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 50], transfer 10 from account 0 to account 0: rejected (rule holds).
Balances [100, 50], transfer 0 from account 1 to account 1: rejected even though the amount is zero (rule holds).
Balances [100, 50], transfer 100 from account 0 to account 0: rejected even though the sender has exactly enough (rule holds).
Balances [5], transfer 1 from account 0 to account 0 on a one-account ledger: rejected (rule holds).
Balances [100, 50], transfer 10 from account 7 to account 7 where account 7 does not exist: rejected (rule holds).

rules.rule: If every balance starts between zero and the maximum, every balance is still between zero and the maximum after any transfer, accepted or not.
intentExamples: Max 1000, balances [990, 20], transfer 20 from account 1 to account 0 is rejected: balances stay [990, 20], all within 0..1000 (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [990, 20], transfer 10 from account 1 to account 0 is accepted: balances become [1000, 10], all within 0..1000 (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [5, 5], transfer 6 from account 0 to account 1 is rejected: no balance goes to -1, they stay [5, 5] (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [5, 5], transfer 5 from account 0 to account 1 is accepted: balances become [0, 10], lowest is exactly 0 (rule holds).
Max 100, balances [100, 100, 0], transfer 100 from account 0 to account 2 is accepted: balances become [0, 100, 100], none above 100 (rule holds).

rules.rule: The number of transfers an in-order batch reports as applied is never more than the number of transfers in the batch.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 0], batch of 3 transfers of 10 from account 0 to account 1, all fine: reports 3 applied, which is not more than 3 (rule holds).
Balances [15, 0], batch of 3 transfers of 10 from account 0 to account 1: the second is rejected, reports 1 applied, which is not more than 3 (rule holds).
Balances [0, 0], batch of 2 transfers of 5 from account 0 to account 1: the first is rejected, reports 0 applied (rule holds).
Any ledger with an empty batch: reports 0 applied, equal to the batch length 0 (rule holds).
Balances [100, 0], batch of 5 transfers where the fourth names missing account 9: reports 3 applied, not more than 5 (rule holds).

rules.rule: Applying a batch as a whole is accepted exactly when applying the same batch in order would apply every transfer, and in that case both leave the ledger with the same balances.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 0], batch [10 from 0 to 1, 20 from 0 to 1]: in-order applies 2 of 2 giving [70, 30]; as a whole is accepted giving [70, 30] (rule holds).
Balances [15, 0], batch [10 from 0 to 1, 10 from 0 to 1]: in-order applies only 1 of 2; as a whole is rejected and balances stay [15, 0] (rule holds).

Balances [0, 50], batch [20 from 1 to 0, 20 from 0 to 1]: in-order applies 2 of 2 giving [0, 50]; as a whole is accepted giving [0, 50], because the second transfer is funded by the first (rule holds).
Balances [30, 30], empty batch: in-order applies 0 of 0; as a whole is accepted and balances stay [30, 30] (rule holds).
Balances [100, 0], batch [10 from 0 to 1, 5 from 1 to 1]: in-order applies 1 of 2; as a whole is rejected and balances stay [100, 0] (rule holds).

rules.rule: No transfer or batch, accepted or rejected, ever adds or removes an account from the ledger.
intentExamples: Ledger with 2 accounts [100, 50], accepted transfer of 30 from account 0 to account 1: still exactly 2 accounts (rule holds).
Ledger with 2 accounts [100, 50], transfer of 10 to missing account 2 is rejected: still 2 accounts, account 2 is not created (rule holds).
Ledger with 3 accounts [10, 0, 0], transfer of 10 from account 0 to account 1 empties account 0: still 3 accounts, account 0 exists with balance 0 (rule holds).
Ledger with 4 accounts, in-order batch of 5 transfers that stops after 2: still 4 accounts (rule holds).
Ledger with 0 accounts, any transfer is rejected: still 0 accounts (rule holds).

rules.rule: A transfer is accepted exactly when both accounts exist, they are different, the sender has at least the amount, and the receiver's balance plus the amount does not exceed the maximum.
intentExamples: Max 1000, balances [100, 50], transfer 100 from account 0 to account 1: all four conditions met (sender has exactly 100), so accepted (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [100, 50], transfer 101 from account 0 to account 1: sender one short, so rejected (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [100, 950], transfer 50 from account 0 to account 1: receiver reaches exactly 1000, so accepted (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [100, 950], transfer 51 from account 0 to account 1: receiver would reach 1001, so rejected (rule holds).
Max 1000, balances [100, 50], transfer 10 from account 0 to account 2: account 2 does not exist, so rejected (rule holds).

rules.rule: A transfer of amount zero is always rejected.
intentExamples: Balances [100, 50], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 1: both exist, differ, sender has enough, receiver does not overflow, so it is accepted and the rule is false here.
Balances [0, 0], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 1: sender has at least 0, so it is accepted and the rule is false here.
Max 1000, balances [5, 1000], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 1: receiver stays at exactly 1000, so it is accepted and the rule is false here.
Balances [100, 50], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 0: rejected, but only because it is a self-transfer (rule happens to hold here).
Balances [100, 50], transfer 0 from account 0 to account 9: rejected, but only because account 9 is missing (rule happens to hold here).

rules.rule: When an in-order batch stops early because a transfer is rejected, the ledger ends up exactly as it was before the batch started.
intentExamples: Balances [15, 0], batch [10 from 0 to 1, 10 from 0 to 1]: stops at the second, reports 1 applied, balances are [5, 10] not [15, 0], so the rule is false here.
Balances [100, 0], batch [40 from 0 to 1, 40 from 0 to 1, 40 from 0 to 1]: stops at the third, balances are [20, 80] not [100, 0], so the rule is false here.
Balances [100, 0], batch [10 from 0 to 1, 5 from 0 to 7]: stops at the second (missing account), balances are [90, 10] not [100, 0], so the rule is false here.
Balances [0, 0], batch [5 from 0 to 1, 5 from 1 to 0]: stops at the very first transfer, 0 applied, balances still [0, 0] (rule happens to hold here).
Max 100, balances [50, 90], batch [10 from 0 to 1, 10 from 0 to 1]: stops at the second (receiver would be 110), balances are [40, 100] not [50, 90], so the rule is false here.

rules.rule: Applying two transfers one after the other gives the same final balances whichever of the two goes first.
intentExamples: Balances [0, 50], A = 20 from account 1 to account 0, B = 20 from account 0 to account 1: A then B gives [0, 50] (both accepted); B then A gives [20, 30] (B rejected, A accepted), so the rule is false here.
Balances [10, 0, 0], A = 10 from 0 to 1, B = 10 from 0 to 2: A then B gives [0, 10, 0]; B then A gives [0, 0, 10], so the rule is false here.
Max 100, balances [50, 95, 50], A = 10 from 0 to 1, B = 10 from 1 to 2: A then B gives [50, 85, 60] (A rejected for overflow, B accepted); B then A gives [40, 95, 60], so the rule is false here.
Balances [100, 100, 100, 100], A = 10 from 0 to 1, B = 10 from 2 to 3: either order gives [90, 110, 90, 110] (rule happens to hold here).
Balances [5, 0], A = 5 from 0 to 1, B = 5 from 1 to 0: A then B gives [5, 0]; B then A gives [0, 5] (B rejected first, then A accepted), so the rule is false here.
